# ---- Cached preparation outputs ----
# here::here() builds paths from the project root (the folder holding the
# .Rproj file and this README), so they resolve the same whether the report is
# knitted or chunks are run interactively. P1-P3 write their outputs to output/.
OUTPUT_DIR <- here::here("output")
P1_PATH <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "P1_cbbc_prepared.rds")
P2_PATH <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "P2_bam_matched.rds")
P3_PATH <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "P3_napops_corrections.rds")
P4_PATH <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "P4_pif_corrections.rds")

# ---- Map ----
BCR_PATH <- "C:/Users/IlesD/OneDrive - EC-EC/Iles/Data/BCR_2026/bcr_2026g.gpkg"   # base map; skipped if absent
MAP_CRS  <- 3978                   # NAD83 / Canada Atlas Lambert
MAP_PAD_M <- 2e5                   # map extent padding around the sites (m)

# ---- Summaries ----
N_BOOT          <- 1000            # bootstrap resamples (sites or species) for CIs
SEED            <- 1
MIN_SITE_SPECIES <- 5              # per-site composition correlation: species non-zero in either dataset

# ---- Site-level regression (section 'Which plots disagree most?') ----
LARGE_PLOT_HA <- 16                # leverage check: refit without plots larger than this (ha)

# ---- CBBC species lists ----
# FALSE: a species missing from an incomplete census list (fewer species rows
# than TOTSPP, or TOTSPP not given) is unknown (NA), not absent. TRUE treats it
# as absent (zero), as a sensitivity check.
ZERO_FILL_INCOMPLETE_LISTS <- FALSE

# ---- Figures ----
REF_FOLDS     <- c(2, 5, 10)       # reference lines at x and 1/x
REF_LINETYPES <- c("dashed", "longdash", "dotted")
REF_CAPTION   <- "Reference lines: solid = agreement; dashed = 2x; long-dash = 5x; dotted = 10x"
RATIO_BREAKS  <- sort(c(1 / 100, 1 / REF_FOLDS, 1, REF_FOLDS, 100))
CLASS_COLOURS <- c(Comparable = "#0072B2", `Non-comparable` = "#E69F00")   # Okabe-Ito blue / orange
CLASS_SHAPES  <- c(Comparable = 17, `Non-comparable` = 16)

# ---- PIF vs NA-POPS corrections ----
# Effective-area column (from P3 or P4) used by each set of corrections. The
# two hybrids swap one component at a time.
CORRECTION_SETS <- c(`NA-POPS`                        = "area_km2",
                     `PIF`                            = "area_pif_km2",
                     `PIF time of day + NA-POPS EDR`  = "area_tod_edr_km2",
                     `NA-POPS availability + PIF MDD` = "area_p_mdd_km2")
CORRECTION_COLOURS <- c(`NA-POPS` = "#0072B2", PIF = "#D55E00")   # Okabe-Ito blue / vermillion
CORRECTION_SHAPES  <- c(`NA-POPS` = 16, PIF = 17)

```{r helpers, include = FALSE, calc = TRUE}
# ---- Statistics ----

# 95% percentile CI for a ratio of means (num / den), resampling sites
boot_ratio_ci <- function(num, den, n_boot = N_BOOT) {
  idx <- matrix(data = sample.int(n = length(num), size = length(num) * n_boot, replace = TRUE), ncol = n_boot)
  r   <- colSums(matrix(data = num[idx], ncol = n_boot)) / colSums(matrix(data = den[idx], ncol = n_boot))
  quantile(x = r[is.finite(r)], probs = c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE)
}

# Species-level ratio of mean densities (num / den) across sites, with a
# site-bootstrap CI and the Spearman correlation across sites
ratio_summary <- function(df, num, den, by = c("species", "comparable")) {
  df |>
    mutate(.num = {{ num }}, .den = {{ den }}) |>
    filter(!is.na(.num), !is.na(.den)) |>
    group_by(across(all_of(by))) |>
    summarise(n_sites   = n(),
              n_den_pos = sum(.den > 0),
              n_num_pos = sum(.num > 0),
              num_mean  = mean(.num),
              den_mean  = mean(.den),
              ratio     = num_mean / den_mean,
              ci        = list(boot_ratio_ci(num = .num, den = .den)),
              spearman  = suppressWarnings(cor(x = .num, y = .den, method = "spearman")),
              .groups   = "drop") |>
    mutate(ratio_lcl     = map_dbl(.x = ci, .f = 1),
           ratio_ucl     = map_dbl(.x = ci, .f = 2),
           ci            = NULL,
           species_class = if_else(condition = comparable, true = "Comparable", false = "Non-comparable"))
}

# Typical ratio, median fold difference from agreement in either direction,
# and share of species within 2x, 5x and 10x
agreement_summary <- function(df) {
  df |>
    filter(is.finite(ratio)) |>   # ratio = 0 counts as outside 10x
    summarise(n_species       = n(),
              median_ratio    = median(ratio),
              median_abs_fold = exp(median(abs(log(ratio)))),
              within_2x       = mean(abs(log(ratio)) <= log(2)),
              within_5x    = mean(abs(log(ratio)) <= log(5)),
              within_10x   = mean(abs(log(ratio)) <= log(10)),
              median_rho   = median(spearman, na.rm = TRUE))
}

# Correlation across species between two abundance measures: Pearson on log
# scale (species positive in both) and Spearman (all species)
cor_summary <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- x > 0 & y > 0
  tibble(n_species   = length(x),
         pearson_log = cor(x = log(x[ok]), y = log(y[ok])),
         spearman    = cor(x = x, y = y, method = "spearman"))
}

# Bootstrap (over species) 95% CI for the change in correlation with `y` when
# measure x1 is replaced by x2
boot_cor_diff <- function(y, x1, x2, n_boot = N_BOOT) {
  d <- replicate(n = n_boot, expr = {
    i  <- sample.int(n = length(y), replace = TRUE)
    ok <- y[i] > 0 & x1[i] > 0 & x2[i] > 0
    c(pearson_log = cor(log(x2[i][ok]), log(y[i][ok])) - cor(log(x1[i][ok]), log(y[i][ok])),
      spearman    = cor(x2[i], y[i], method = "spearman") - cor(x1[i], y[i], method = "spearman"))
  })
  tibble(measure = rownames(d),
         lcl     = apply(X = d, MARGIN = 1, FUN = quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
         ucl     = apply(X = d, MARGIN = 1, FUN = quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))
}

# Quantile summary of numeric columns, one row per column
quantile_table <- function(df, cols) {
  df |>
    select(all_of(cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "variable") |>
    group_by(variable) |>
    summarise(min = min(value), q25 = quantile(value, 0.25), median = median(value),
              q75 = quantile(value, 0.75), max = max(value), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = cols)) |>
    arrange(variable)
}

# Ratio estimator of density from a set of surveys: total count / total
# effective area, using only surveys that have an effective area (NA if none)
ratio_estimate <- function(count, area) {
  has_area <- !is.na(area)
  if (!any(has_area)) return(NA_real_)
  sum(count[has_area]) / sum(area[has_area])
}

# ---- Count ratio (birds counted / birds expected) ----
#
# See section "How the absolute comparisons work" in the report.
# If CBBC density D and the NA-POPS corrections are both right, the expected
# count of survey j near site i is
#   E[count_ij] = k x area_ij x D_cbbc_i,   with k = 1
#     area_ij   NA-POPS effective area of the survey (km^2)
#     D_cbbc_i  CBBC territory density at the site (territories / km^2)
#     k         observed / expected: birds counted per bird predicted from
#               CBBC territories and the corrections (1 = agreement)
#   k = total observed count / total expected count
# which is the Poisson maximum-likelihood estimate of k. Surveys at grids with
# no CBBC territories of the species have an expected count of 0, so their
# birds add to the observed total only.
# 95% sampling interval: the wider of
#   - a site bootstrap (sites resampled with all their surveys, which keeps
#     repeat visits and nearby points together and absorbs overdispersion).
#     Resamples that draw only grids without CBBC territories give an
#     undefined ratio (0/0 or x/0) and are dropped, as in boot_ratio_ci();
#     n_boot_undefined records how many; and
#   - the exact Poisson interval for the total count, divided by the expected
#     count, which gives a non-zero upper bound when no birds were counted
#     (where every bootstrap resample would be zero).
# Both are conditional on the NA-POPS corrections and CBBC densities.
count_ratio_summary <- function(df, n_boot = N_BOOT) {
  species_list <- sort(unique(df$species))
  results <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(species_list))

  for (i in seq_along(species_list)) {
    d <- df[df$species == species_list[i], ]
    d$expected <- d$area_km2 * d$cbbc_dens_km2

    # Site bootstrap of observed / expected
    rows_by_site <- split(x = seq_len(nrow(d)), f = d$SITEID)
    k_boot <- rep(NA_real_, n_boot)
    for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
      sampled_sites <- sample(x = names(rows_by_site), size = length(rows_by_site), replace = TRUE)
      rows <- unlist(rows_by_site[sampled_sites], use.names = FALSE)
      k_boot[b] <- sum(d$count[rows]) / sum(d$expected[rows])
    }

    # Exact Poisson 95% interval for the total count, divided by the expected count
    observed_total <- sum(d$count)
    expected_total <- sum(d$expected)
    poisson_lcl <- if (observed_total == 0) 0 else qchisq(p = 0.025, df = 2 * observed_total) / 2 / expected_total
    poisson_ucl <- qchisq(p = 0.975, df = 2 * (observed_total + 1)) / 2 / expected_total

    # Share of the expected count contributed by the species' largest site:
    # a large share means one site dominates the count ratio
    site_expected <- tapply(X = d$expected, INDEX = d$SITEID, FUN = sum)

    results[[i]] <- tibble(
      species          = species_list[i],
      comparable       = d$comparable[1],
      n_sites          = n_distinct(d$SITEID),
      n_sites_cbbc     = n_distinct(d$SITEID[d$cbbc_dens_km2 > 0]),
      n_surveys        = nrow(d),
      observed         = observed_total,
      expected         = expected_total,
      k                = observed_total / expected_total,
      k_lcl            = min(quantile(x = k_boot[is.finite(k_boot)], probs = 0.025, names = FALSE), poisson_lcl),
      k_ucl            = max(quantile(x = k_boot[is.finite(k_boot)], probs = 0.975, names = FALSE), poisson_ucl),
      n_boot_undefined = sum(!is.finite(k_boot)),
      max_site_share   = max(site_expected) / sum(d$expected)
    )
  }

  bind_rows(results) |>
    mutate(species_class = if_else(condition = comparable, true = "Comparable", false = "Non-comparable"))
}

# Summary of count ratios across species: median, median fold difference in
# either direction, share within 2x / 5x of agreement, and the number of
# species with no birds counted (k = 0, which counts as outside 5x)
count_ratio_agreement <- function(df) {
  df |>
    filter(is.finite(k)) |>
    summarise(n_species       = n(),
              median_k        = median(k),
              median_abs_fold = exp(median(abs(log(k)))),
              within_2x       = mean(abs(log(k)) <= log(2)),
              within_5x       = mean(abs(log(k)) <= log(5)),
              n_no_birds      = sum(k == 0))
}

# ---- Leverage check for the plot-size term ----

# log(plot size) coefficient of a site-level regression, fitted to all sites and
# refitted without plots larger than LARGE_PLOT_HA
plot_size_leverage <- function(fit, data) {
  fit_small <- update(object = fit, data = filter(data, plot_ha <= LARGE_PLOT_HA))
  plot_row  <- "log(plot_ha)"
  tibble(sites   = c("All sites", sprintf("Plots <= %g ha", LARGE_PLOT_HA)),
         n_sites = c(nobs(fit), nobs(fit_small)),
         estimate  = c(coef(summary(fit))[plot_row, "Estimate"],   coef(summary(fit_small))[plot_row, "Estimate"]),
         std_error = c(coef(summary(fit))[plot_row, "Std. Error"], coef(summary(fit_small))[plot_row, "Std. Error"]),
         p_value   = c(coef(summary(fit))[plot_row, "Pr(>|t|)"],   coef(summary(fit_small))[plot_row, "Pr(>|t|)"]))
}

# ---- CBBC site densities ----

# Census records whose species list is complete: at least as many species rows
# as TOTSPP says the list should contain. Only these are zero-filled below.
complete_list_records <- p1$cbbc_qa |>
  filter(keep, !is.na(TOTSPP), n_species_rows >= TOTSPP) |>
  pull(RECNO)

# Site densities (territories / km^2) for species `spp` at `sites`, then the
# mean over the site's census years:
#   - a species missing from a complete census list is a zero (absent);
#   - a species missing from an incomplete list (or one without TOTSPP) is
#     unknown (NA), unless ZERO_FILL_INCOMPLETE_LISTS is TRUE;
#   - a species listed without a usable density stays NA (explicit = FALSE);
#   - ALFL / WIFL are unknown in Traill's Flycatcher records.
# The mean over census years uses only the years where the species is known.
cbbc_site_density <- function(spp, sites) {
  p1$cbbc_long |>
    filter(SITEID %in% sites) |>
    select(RECNO, SITEID, YEAR, species, dens_km2) |>
    mutate(listed = TRUE) |>
    complete(nesting(RECNO, SITEID, YEAR), species = spp, fill = list(dens_km2 = 0), explicit = FALSE) |>
    filter(species %in% spp) |>
    mutate(dens_km2 = if_else(condition = is.na(listed) & !RECNO %in% complete_list_records & !ZERO_FILL_INCOMPLETE_LISTS,
                              true = NA_real_, false = dens_km2),
           dens_km2 = if_else(condition = RECNO %in% p1$traill_records & species %in% s1$traill_species,
                              true = NA_real_, false = dens_km2)) |>
    group_by(SITEID, species) |>
    summarise(n_census       = sum(!is.na(dens_km2)),
              cbbc_dens_km2  = mean(dens_km2, na.rm = TRUE),
              cbbc_year_mean = mean(YEAR),
              .groups        = "drop") |>
    filter(!is.nan(cbbc_dens_km2))
}

# ---- Figures ----

ref_vlines <- function() {
  c(list(geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "grey30")),
    map2(.x = REF_FOLDS, .y = REF_LINETYPES,
         .f = ~ geom_vline(xintercept = c(1 / .x, .x), linetype = .y, colour = "grey55")))
}
ref_ablines <- function() {
  c(list(geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, colour = "grey30")),
    map2(.x = REF_FOLDS, .y = REF_LINETYPES,
         .f = ~ geom_abline(intercept = log10(c(1 / .x, .x)), slope = 1, linetype = .y, colour = "grey55")))
}
fold_labels <- function(x) if_else(condition = x < 1, true = paste0("1/", round(1 / x)), false = as.character(x))

# Species ratios with 95% CIs, sorted, against the reference lines
plot_ratio <- function(summary, xlab) {
  summary |>
    filter(is.finite(ratio), ratio > 0) |>
    mutate(species = fct_reorder(.f = species, .x = ratio)) |>
    ggplot(mapping = aes(x = ratio, y = species, colour = species_class, shape = species_class)) +
    ref_vlines() +
    geom_linerange(mapping = aes(xmin = pmax(ratio_lcl, min(RATIO_BREAKS)), xmax = ratio_ucl)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = RATIO_BREAKS, labels = fold_labels) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = CLASS_COLOURS) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = CLASS_SHAPES) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL, caption = REF_CAPTION) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}

# Log-log scatter of two species-level measures with labels and reference lines
plot_pair <- function(df, x, y, xlab, ylab, ref = TRUE) {
  df |>
    filter(.data[[x]] > 0, .data[[y]] > 0) |>
    ggplot(mapping = aes(x = .data[[x]], y = .data[[y]], colour = species_class, shape = species_class)) +
    (if (ref) ref_ablines() else NULL) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_text(mapping = aes(label = species), size = 2.2, vjust = -0.7, check_overlap = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_y_log10() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = CLASS_COLOURS) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = CLASS_SHAPES) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, colour = NULL, shape = NULL, caption = if (ref) REF_CAPTION else NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}

fig_height <- function(n) 1.5 + 0.14 * n   # height for one-row-per-species figures

pct <- function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%")
```

```{r build-tables, include = FALSE, calc = TRUE}
# ---- Sites ----
# P2 has excluded entire shared-coordinate CBBC groups and assigned each BAM
# survey to its nearest remaining site. These final sites define BOTH species
# selection (P3) and all report calculations.
if (!isTRUE(s2$exclude_shared_coordinates) ||
    !isTRUE(s2$assign_nearest_before_species_selection)) {
  stop("Cached preparation outputs use old matching rules: rerun P1-P4.")
}
if (!is.numeric(s3$min_sites_cbbc) || length(s3$min_sites_cbbc) != 1L ||
    is.na(s3$min_sites_cbbc) || s3$min_sites_cbbc < 1 ||
    s3$min_sites_cbbc != as.integer(s3$min_sites_cbbc)) {
  stop("P3 cached output has no valid min_sites_cbbc setting: rerun P3-P4.")
}
matched_sites <- unique(p2$site_survey$SITEID)
if (any(matched_sites %in% p1$cbbc_sites$SITEID[p1$cbbc_sites$shared_coords])) {
  stop("Shared-coordinate site appeared in the final matched-site set.")
}

sites_info <- p1$cbbc_sites |>
  mutate(matched = SITEID %in% matched_sites)

# ---- Candidate species ----
# All species with CBBC territories at enough matched sites and an NA-POPS
# model, whether or not BAM detected them (P3). Narrowed to those with NA-POPS models
# below, once the quantities used to select it have been computed.
cands          <- p3$species_candidates
if (anyNA(cands$comparable) ||
    any(cands$comparable != !(cands$species %in% s1$non_comparable_species))) {
  stop("P3 cached species classes disagree with P1; rerun P1, then P3 and P4 before knitting.")
}
spp_candidates <- cands |> filter(in_napops) |> pull(species)

# ---- Survey assignment (every comparison) ----
# P2 already excluded shared-coordinate groups AND assigned each survey once;
# re-assignment here would create inconsistency with P3 species selection.
survey_nearest <- p2$site_survey
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(survey_nearest$survey_id))
survey_grid <- survey_nearest |>
  transmute(SITEID, survey_id, year, site_year = paste(location_id, year, sep = "_"))

n_sites_assigned <- n_distinct(survey_grid$SITEID)
exclusion_audit <- p2$exclusion_audit
n_shared_sites_excluded <- exclusion_audit$excluded_cbbc_sites_with_surveys
n_shared_groups_excluded <- exclusion_audit$excluded_coordinate_groups_with_surveys
n_surveys_lost_shared <- exclusion_audit$surveys_without_unambiguous_site

# ---- Matched site x species table (steps 1 and 3) ----
# BAM: count per survey (uncorrected) and NA-POPS-corrected density (ratio
# estimator over the surveys assigned to the site).
# Every matched site x species combination is kept, including grids where
# spot mapping found no territories of the species (CBBC density 0; see
# section 'Data and matching').
site_bam <- survey_grid |>
  select(SITEID, survey_id, year) |>
  inner_join(y = select(p3$survey_species, survey_id, species, count, area_km2),
             by = "survey_id") |>
  group_by(SITEID, species) |>
  summarise(n_surveys     = n(),
            sum_count     = sum(count),
            bam_dens_km2  = ratio_estimate(count = count, area = area_km2),
            bam_year_mean = mean(year),
            .groups       = "drop") |>
  mutate(count_per_survey = sum_count / n_surveys)

# Site x species combinations where the CBBC density is known (not missing
# from an incomplete census list), including CBBC zeros
site_matched_all <- site_bam |>
  inner_join(y = cbbc_site_density(spp = spp_candidates, sites = matched_sites), by = c("SITEID", "species")) |>
  filter(!is.na(cbbc_dens_km2)) |>
  mutate(comparable = !species %in% s1$non_comparable_species)

# The same rows, with plot attributes for the comparisons and the site regression
site_matched <- site_matched_all |>
  left_join(y = select(sites_info, SITEID, plot_ha, visits_mean), by = "SITEID") |>
  mutate(year_gap = bam_year_mean - cbbc_year_mean)

# ---- Survey-level table ----
# One row per retained survey x NA-POPS species, at all of the species' matched
# grids (same survey assignment as above).
survey_data <- survey_grid |>
  inner_join(y = select(p3$survey_species, survey_id, species, count, area_km2), by = "survey_id") |>
  filter(species %in% spp_candidates, !is.na(area_km2)) |>
  inner_join(y = select(site_matched, SITEID, species, cbbc_dens_km2, cbbc_year_mean, comparable),
             by = c("SITEID", "species"))

# ---- Species compared ----
# Every candidate from P3 (CBBC territories at >= s3$min_sites_cbbc of the FINAL sites,
# after the coordinate exclusion and nearest-site assignment in P2) that
# has NA-POPS removal and distance models. No other
# criterion is applied. Availability, EDR and the BAM count expected under
# agreement are computed for reference only.

# Availability standardized to a 5-min count (same cue rate, survey's own p
# rescaled from its duration)
availability_5min <- p3$survey_species |>
  filter(species %in% spp_candidates, !is.na(p)) |>
  mutate(p_5min = 1 - (1 - p)^(5 / (duration / 60))) |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(p_5min_median = median(p_5min), .groups = "drop")

# BAM count expected if NA-POPS-corrected densities equalled CBBC densities
# (see section "Species compared")
expected_counts <- survey_data |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(expected_count = sum(area_km2 * cbbc_dens_km2),
            observed_count = sum(count),
            .groups        = "drop")

species_selection <- cands |>
  select(species, common_name, family, n_sites_cbbc, in_napops, comparable, detected_nearby) |>
  left_join(y = availability_5min, by = "species") |>
  left_join(y = select(p3$species_corrections, species, edr_m), by = "species") |>
  left_join(y = expected_counts, by = "species") |>
  mutate(primary = in_napops)

spp_primary <- species_selection |> filter(primary) |> pull(species)

# ---- Restrict every comparison to the species compared ----
spp_napops   <- spp_primary
site_matched     <- filter(site_matched, species %in% spp_primary)
site_matched_all <- filter(site_matched_all, species %in% spp_primary)
survey_data      <- filter(survey_data, species %in% spp_primary)

# ---- CBBC census filters and matched sites ----

# ---- Site map ----

  mutate(status = if_else(condition = matched, true = sprintf("Matched (BAM surveys within %g km)", s2$match_radius_m / 1000), false = "Not matched")) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>

```{r calc-corrections, include = FALSE, calc = TRUE}
corr_tbl <- p3$species_corrections |>
  filter(species %in% spp_napops) |>
  mutate(density_ci_factor = (edr_ucl / edr_lcl)^2)   # width of the density interval from EDR sampling error alone

napops_surveys <- p3$survey_species |> filter(species %in% spp_napops, !is.na(area_km2))

# Share of the variation in log effective area (across all survey x species
# combinations) explained by species alone; the rest is variation among
# surveys of the same species
r2_species <- summary(lm(formula = log(area_km2) ~ species, data = napops_surveys))$r.squared

# Within-species spread: effective area of the 90th vs 10th percentile survey,
# median across species
within_species_fold <- median(corr_tbl$area_q90_km2 / corr_tbl$area_q10_km2, na.rm = TRUE)
area_range <- range(corr_tbl$area_median_km2)
var_edr    <- var(log(pi * corr_tbl$edr_m^2))
var_p      <- var(log(corr_tbl$p_median))

# How much the correction re-ranks species: uncorrected vs corrected mean
# abundance across species at all matched grids
rerank <- site_matched |>
  filter(species %in% spp_napops, !is.na(bam_dens_km2)) |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(count = mean(count_per_survey), dens = mean(bam_dens_km2), .groups = "drop")
rho_rerank <- cor(x = rerank$count, y = rerank$dens, method = "spearman")

# Key features of the corrections, for the table in Section 'NA-POPS detectability corrections'
corrections_features <- tibble(
  feature = c("Spread of median effective area across species (max / min)",
              "Share of variance in log effective area due to species identity",
              "Share of between-species variance in log(p x EDR^2) from EDR",
              "Spearman rank correlation, uncorrected vs corrected species abundance",
              "Median width of density 95% interval from EDR sampling error alone (factor; excludes model, release and availability uncertainty)",
              "Median share of surveys outside NA-POPS training range"),
  value = c(sprintf("%.1f", area_range[2] / area_range[1]),
            pct(r2_species),
            pct(var_edr / (var_edr + var_p)),
            sprintf("%.2f", rho_rerank),
            sprintf("%.2f", median(corr_tbl$density_ci_factor, na.rm = TRUE)),
            pct(median(pmax(corr_tbl$share_od_out, corr_tbl$share_tssr_out))))
)
```

```{r calc-composition, include = FALSE, calc = TRUE}
# ---- Uncorrected composition: within-site shares ----
# Step 1: each species' share of each site's community, in each dataset.
# Sites where either dataset recorded none of the species compared are dropped,
# so both datasets' shares are averaged over the same sites.
site_shares <- site_matched_all |>
  group_by(SITEID) |>
  filter(sum(cbbc_dens_km2) > 0, sum(count_per_survey) > 0) |>
  mutate(cbbc_site_share = cbbc_dens_km2 / sum(cbbc_dens_km2),
         bam_site_share  = count_per_survey / sum(count_per_survey)) |>
  ungroup()

# Step 2: average each species' shares across sites (0 where it was absent)
rel_abund <- site_shares |>
  group_by(species, comparable) |>
  summarise(cbbc_share = mean(cbbc_site_share),
            bam_share  = mean(bam_site_share),
            .groups    = "drop") |>
  mutate(species_class = if_else(condition = comparable, true = "Comparable", false = "Non-comparable"))

n_share_sites <- n_distinct(site_shares$SITEID)

cor_1e <- bind_rows(`All species` = cor_summary(x = rel_abund$cbbc_share, y = rel_abund$bam_share),
                    `Comparable` = with(filter(rel_abund, comparable), cor_summary(x = cbbc_share, y = bam_share)),
                    .id = "species")

# Per site: rank correlation across species of CBBC density and BAM count per survey
site_composition <- site_matched_all |>
  group_by(SITEID) |>
  filter(sum(cbbc_dens_km2 > 0 | count_per_survey > 0) >= MIN_SITE_SPECIES) |>
  summarise(rho = suppressWarnings(cor(x = cbbc_dens_km2, y = count_per_survey, method = "spearman")),
            .groups = "drop")

# ---- Corrected composition: species means, uncorrected vs NA-POPS-corrected ----
# `four` (site x species, NA-POPS species with a corrected density) is also
# the input to the plot-averaged density ratio and the site regression
four <- site_matched |> filter(species %in% spp_napops, !is.na(bam_dens_km2))

means_4 <- four |>
  group_by(species, comparable) |>
  summarise(cbbc = mean(cbbc_dens_km2), uncorrected = mean(count_per_survey),
            corrected = mean(bam_dens_km2), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(species_class = if_else(condition = comparable, true = "Comparable", false = "Non-comparable"))

cor_4a <- bind_rows(
  `Uncorrected, all`         = cor_summary(x = means_4$cbbc, y = means_4$uncorrected),
  `Corrected, all`           = cor_summary(x = means_4$cbbc, y = means_4$corrected),
  `Uncorrected, comparable` = with(filter(means_4, comparable), cor_summary(x = cbbc, y = uncorrected)),
  `Corrected, comparable`   = with(filter(means_4, comparable), cor_summary(x = cbbc, y = corrected)),
  .id = "BAM point counts"
)

cor_change <- with(filter(means_4, comparable), boot_cor_diff(y = cbbc, x1 = uncorrected, x2 = corrected))

# How much comparable species differ in raw counts and in CBBC density,
# compared with how much their NA-POPS corrections (median effective area) differ
species_spread <- means_4 |>
  filter(comparable, uncorrected > 0) |>
  left_join(y = select(corr_tbl, species, area_median_km2, edr_m), by = "species")

count_fold        <- max(species_spread$uncorrected) / min(species_spread$uncorrected)
cbbc_fold         <- max(species_spread$cbbc) / min(species_spread$cbbc)
correction_fold   <- max(species_spread$area_median_km2) / min(species_spread$area_median_km2)
edr_range_m       <- range(species_spread$edr_m)
sd_log_count      <- sd(log(species_spread$uncorrected))
sd_log_correction <- sd(log(species_spread$area_median_km2))

# Comparable species with the largest EDRs (largest effective areas, so the
# correction lowers their densities most)
largest_edr_species <- species_spread |> arrange(desc(edr_m)) |> slice_head(n = 3) |> pull(species)

# ---- Count ratio vs plot-averaged density ratio, by species ----
ratio_pairs <- count_ratio |>
  select(species, species_class, count_ratio = k, max_site_share, n_sites_cbbc) |>
  inner_join(y = select(density_ratio, species, density_ratio = ratio), by = "species") |>
  mutate(fold_apart = count_ratio / density_ratio)

# ---- Population change since the census ----
# Median census-to-survey gap per species, across its matched grids
year_gap_species <- survey_data |>
  group_by(species, SITEID) |>
  summarise(year_gap = mean(year) - first(cbbc_year_mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(median_year_gap = median(year_gap), .groups = "drop")

time_data <- density_ratio |>
  filter(is.finite(ratio), ratio > 0) |>
  left_join(y = year_gap_species, by = "species")

# ---- Detection-rate check ----
# Detection frequency at all matched grids. A single survey's count is
# Poisson(D x area) if CBBC density and the corrections are right, so
# P(detected) = 1 - exp(-D x area). Evaluated per survey, not per site,
# because repeat visits to the same point re-survey the same birds and are not
# independent draws.
detection_check <- survey_data |>
  filter(comparable) |>
  mutate(detected     = count > 0,
         p_detect_exp = 1 - exp(-cbbc_dens_km2 * area_km2)) |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(n_surveys  = n(),
            detect_obs = mean(detected),
            detect_exp = mean(p_detect_exp),
            .groups    = "drop") |>
  mutate(obs_over_exp = detect_obs / detect_exp)

detection_summary <- detection_check |>
  summarise(n_species            = n(),
            median_detect_obs    = median(detect_obs),
            median_detect_exp    = median(detect_exp),
            median_obs_over_exp  = median(obs_over_exp),
            share_obs_below_exp  = mean(detect_obs < detect_exp))

# ---- Site-level regression: which plots disagree most ----
community_4 <- four |>
  filter(comparable) |>
  group_by(SITEID, plot_ha, visits_mean, cbbc_year_mean) |>
  summarise(bam_total = sum(bam_dens_km2), cbbc_total = sum(cbbc_dens_km2), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(bam_total > 0, cbbc_total > 0) |>
  mutate(community_ratio = bam_total / cbbc_total)

fit_4c <- lm(formula = log(community_ratio) ~ log(visits_mean) + log(plot_ha) + I(cbbc_year_mean - 1975),
             data = community_4)

```{r calc-pif, include = FALSE, calc = TRUE}
# Surveys and grids as for the NA-POPS comparisons (survey_data: all matched
# grids), restricted to species with PIF values, with the alternative
# effective areas from P4
pif_survey_data <- survey_data |>
  inner_join(y = p4$survey_species, by = c("survey_id", "species"))

n_pif_species <- n_distinct(pif_survey_data$species)

# ---- Plot-averaged density ratio with each set of corrections (main) ----
# For each set: corrected density at each grid with the set's effective areas
# (ratio estimator over the grid's surveys), then the mean across grids divided
# by the mean CBBC density across the same grids, as for NA-POPS
pif_density_ratio <- list()
for (set_name in names(CORRECTION_SETS)) {
  d <- pif_survey_data
  d$area_set_km2 <- d[[CORRECTION_SETS[[set_name]]]]

  grid_density <- d |>
    group_by(SITEID, species, comparable) |>
    summarise(bam_dens_km2  = ratio_estimate(count = count, area = area_set_km2),
              cbbc_dens_km2 = first(cbbc_dens_km2),
              .groups       = "drop")

  pif_density_ratio[[set_name]] <- ratio_summary(df = grid_density, num = bam_dens_km2, den = cbbc_dens_km2)
}
pif_density_ratio <- bind_rows(pif_density_ratio, .id = "correction") |>
  mutate(correction = factor(correction, levels = names(CORRECTION_SETS)))

# ---- Count ratio with each set of corrections (check) ----
# The set's effective-area column is copied to area_km2, the column
# count_ratio_summary() uses
pif_count_ratio <- list()
for (set_name in names(CORRECTION_SETS)) {
  d <- pif_survey_data
  d$area_km2 <- d[[CORRECTION_SETS[[set_name]]]]
  pif_count_ratio[[set_name]] <- count_ratio_summary(df = d)
}
pif_count_ratio <- bind_rows(pif_count_ratio, .id = "correction") |>
  mutate(correction = factor(correction, levels = names(CORRECTION_SETS)))

# ---- Birds expected with each alternative, relative to NA-POPS ----
expected_vs_napops <- pif_count_ratio |>
  filter(comparable) |>
  select(species, correction, expected) |>
  group_by(species) |>
  mutate(relative = expected / expected[correction == "NA-POPS"]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(correction != "NA-POPS")


# ---- Agreement with CBBC under each set of corrections (main) ----
pif_agreement <- bind_rows(
  `Comparable` = pif_density_ratio |> filter(comparable) |> group_by(correction) |> agreement_summary(),
  `All species` = pif_density_ratio |> group_by(correction) |> agreement_summary(),
  .id = "subset"
)

# ---- Check: count ratio under each set of corrections ----
pif_count_agreement <- bind_rows(
  `Comparable` = pif_count_ratio |> filter(comparable) |> group_by(correction) |> count_ratio_agreement(),
  `All species` = pif_count_ratio |> group_by(correction) |> count_ratio_agreement(),
  .id = "subset"
)

# ---- NA-POPS vs PIF, species by species ----
# A species is closer to agreement with whichever correction gives the
# plot-averaged density ratio nearer 1 on the log scale. Species with no birds
# counted have a ratio of 0 under both and are left out.
pif_paired <- pif_density_ratio |>
  filter(correction == "NA-POPS") |>
  select(species, comparable, species_class, den_mean, napops_mean = num_mean, r_napops = ratio) |>
  inner_join(y = pif_density_ratio |>
               filter(correction == "PIF") |>
               select(species, r_pif = ratio, r_pif_lcl = ratio_lcl, r_pif_ucl = ratio_ucl),
             by = "species") |>
  left_join(y = select(p4$pif_species, species, pif_tod, pif_mdd_m, pif_pair, edr_m), by = "species") |>
  mutate(closer = case_when(napops_mean == 0 | !is.finite(r_napops)  ~ NA_character_,
                            abs(log(r_pif)) < abs(log(r_napops))     ~ "PIF",
                            .default                                 = "NA-POPS"))

# Comparable species with birds counted: share closer to agreement with PIF,
# with an exact binomial 95% interval
closer_comp  <- pif_paired |> filter(comparable, !is.na(closer))
n_closer_pif <- sum(closer_comp$closer == "PIF")
closer_ci    <- binom.test(x = n_closer_pif, n = nrow(closer_comp))$conf.int

# Results quoted in the text and the synthesis
pif_comp        <- pif_agreement |> filter(subset == "Comparable")
pif_comp_napops <- pif_comp |> filter(correction == "NA-POPS")
pif_comp_pif    <- pif_comp |> filter(correction == "PIF")
pif_count_comp  <- pif_count_agreement |> filter(subset == "Comparable")
pif_rel_median  <- median(expected_vs_napops$relative[expected_vs_napops$correction == "PIF"])

# Species order for the NA-POPS vs PIF figure (comparable species with birds counted)
species_order <- pif_paired |>
  filter(comparable, napops_mean > 0) |>
  arrange(r_napops) |>
  pull(species)

# ---- Composition with PIF corrections ----
# Composition: species mean corrected density across all matched grids (ratio
# estimator at each grid, then the mean across grids) with each set of
# corrections, against mean CBBC density, comparable species
pif_means <- pif_survey_data |>
  filter(comparable) |>
  group_by(SITEID, species) |>
  summarise(cbbc    = first(cbbc_dens_km2),
            napops  = sum(count) / sum(area_km2),
            pif     = sum(count) / sum(area_pif_km2),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(across(.cols = c(cbbc, napops, pif), .fns = mean), .groups = "drop")

cor_pif <- bind_rows(`NA-POPS` = cor_summary(x = pif_means$cbbc, y = pif_means$napops),
                     PIF       = cor_summary(x = pif_means$cbbc, y = pif_means$pif),
                     .id = "corrections")

cor_pif_change <- boot_cor_diff(y = pif_means$cbbc, x1 = pif_means$napops, x2 = pif_means$pif)
```

closer_overall <- if (abs(log(pif_comp_napops$median_ratio)) < abs(log(pif_comp_pif$median_ratio))) "NA-POPS" else "PIF"

# Key results table for the Summary
synthesis <- tribble(
  ~role, ~comparison, ~metric, ~value,

  "Main",        "Plot-averaged density ratio, NA-POPS (comparable species)", "Share within 2x / 10x", paste(pct(comp_density_ratio$within_2x), "/", pct(comp_density_ratio$within_10x)),
  "Main",        "Plot-averaged density ratio, PIF (comparable species with PIF values)", "Median ratio", sprintf("%.2f", pif_comp_pif$median_ratio),
  "Main",        "Plot-averaged density ratio, PIF (comparable species with PIF values)", "Median fold difference (either direction)", sprintf("%.2f", pif_comp_pif$median_abs_fold),
  "Main",        "Plot-averaged density ratio, PIF (comparable species with PIF values)", "Share within 2x / 10x", paste(pct(pif_comp_pif$within_2x), "/", pct(pif_comp_pif$within_10x)),
  "Main",        "PIF vs NA-POPS, plot-averaged density ratio (comparable species)", "Share of species closer to 1 with PIF", pct(n_closer_pif / nrow(closer_comp)),
  "Check",       "Count ratio, NA-POPS (comparable species)", "Median ratio", sprintf("%.2f", comp_count_ratio$median_k),
  "Check",       "Count ratio, NA-POPS (comparable species)", "Share within 2x", pct(comp_count_ratio$within_2x),
  "Check",       "Detection rate (comparable species)", "Observed / expected, median", sprintf("%.2f", detection_summary$median_obs_over_exp),
  "Composition", "CBBC vs BAM uncorrected (all species, all matched sites)", "Spearman, species shares", sprintf("%.2f", cor_1e$spearman[1]),
  "Composition", "CBBC vs BAM NA-POPS-corrected (all species)", "Spearman, species means", sprintf("%.2f", cor_4a$spearman[2])
)

# Summary {#summary}

**What this compares.**
This repository compares two ways of estimating breeding-bird density in Canada:

- **Point counts** from the Boreal Avian Modelling (BAM) Project's point-count database, converted to density with detectability corrections from **NA-POPS** (Point count Offsets for Population Sizes of North American landbirds).
- **Spot mapping** from the **Canadian Breeding Bird Census (CBBC)**, in which observers visited fixed plots repeatedly and mapped territories, giving densities that need no detectability correction.

If the NA-POPS corrections are about right, corrected point counts near CBBC plots should give densities of the same magnitude as the CBBC censuses. It is a plausibility check on the corrections, not a validation of them; the limitations are set out in Section \@ref(ratio-caveats).

**Comparable versus non-comparable species.** The primary analysis focuses on species for which repeated spot mapping can plausibly delineate relatively stable breeding territories, and for which territory density provides a reasonably interpretable reference for NA-POPS-corrected point-count density. **Non-comparable** species are those whose breeding ecology may cause systematic differences between the quantities estimated by the two methods, even with accurate detectability corrections. Examples include birds that defend only nesting sites but forage widely, flocking or nomadic species, birds with ranges much larger than the mapped plots, and species whose territorial signals occur primarily outside the point-count season. These differences may introduce bias of uncertain direction, as well as greater variability in the relationship between point counts and mapped territories. The classification is based on breeding ecology, not on whether observed and expected counts agree. Non-comparable species remain in the data and exploratory all-species results, but are excluded from the primary comparable-species density and PIF comparisons. A brief justification for each flagged species is provided in Section \@ref(noncomparable-justifications).

The same check is repeated with the older **Partners in Flight (PIF)** corrections that NA-POPS replaced in continental population estimates (a time-of-day adjustment instead of availability, and an expert-assigned detection distance instead of EDR), to see which set of corrections brings point counts closer to the CBBC censuses (Section \@ref(pif-vs-napops)).

## Key findings

All results below use **`r n_matched` final CBBC locations**, after excluding CBBC plots with inadequate effort, those with no nearby point counts, and several distinct plots with identical coordinates that could not be uniquely assigned to paired point counts. To be included in this analysis, species must have been observed in **at least `r s3$min_sites_cbbc` of these remaining CBBC locations**. All numerical results below are computed for this restricted sample.

- **NA-POPS-corrected point counts vs spot mapping.** For the `r comp_density_ratio$n_species` comparable species, NA-POPS-corrected point-count density is a median of **`r round(comp_density_ratio$median_ratio, 2)` times** the CBBC territory density (plot-averaged density ratio). Individual species are typically `r round(comp_density_ratio$median_abs_fold, 2)`-fold from agreement in either direction; `r pct(comp_density_ratio$within_2x)` are within 2× and `r pct(comp_density_ratio$within_10x)` within 10× (Section \@ref(plot-averaged)).
- **PIF vs NA-POPS.** The older PIF corrections assume each survey samples a median of `r round(pif_rel_median, 2)` times as many birds as NA-POPS does, so they give lower densities. With PIF the median density ratio is **`r round(pif_comp_pif$median_ratio, 2)`**, against **`r round(pif_comp_napops$median_ratio, 2)`** with NA-POPS, so on the median `r closer_overall` is closer to agreement. PIF is closer for `r n_closer_pif` of `r nrow(closer_comp)` comparable species (Section \@ref(pif-vs-napops)).
- **Composition.** Before any correction, CBBC and BAM relative abundances have a Spearman correlation of `r round(cor_1e$spearman[1], 2)` across species. Uncorrected and NA-POPS-corrected abundance have a Spearman correlation of `r round(rho_rerank, 2)` across species, which measures how much the corrections re-rank species (Section \@ref(composition)).

```{r summary-figure, fig.cap = "Plot-averaged density ratio (NA-POPS- or PIF-corrected point-count density / CBBC territory density) by comparable species, sorted by the NA-POPS ratio. Each line joins one species' two ratios. A ratio of 1 means agreement.", fig.height = fig_height(length(species_order))}
pif_density_ratio |>
  filter(species %in% species_order, correction %in% c("NA-POPS", "PIF")) |>
  mutate(species = factor(species, levels = species_order)) |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = ratio, y = species)) +
  ref_vlines() +
  geom_line(mapping = aes(group = species), colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(colour = correction, shape = correction), size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = RATIO_BREAKS, labels = fold_labels) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = CORRECTION_COLOURS) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = CORRECTION_SHAPES) +
  labs(x = "Plot-averaged density ratio: corrected point-count density / CBBC density", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
       caption = REF_CAPTION) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r summary-table}
kable(synthesis, col.names = c("Role", "Comparison", "Metric", "Value"),
      caption = "Key results (every comparison uses all matched CBBC grids)", label = "summary-1")
```

## How to read these results

This is a plausibility check on the NA-POPS corrections, not a validation of them. A ratio near 1 means corrected point counts give densities of the same magnitude as an independent, intensive census. Even with perfect corrections the ratio need not be 1:

- **Birds vs territories.** Point counts may include non-territorial individuals, while spot mapping records territories, so ratios somewhat above 1 are expected.
- **Time.** The censuses and the point counts are a median of `r round(median(year_gap$gap))` years apart (Section \@ref(timing)), and populations have changed in between.
- **Habitat.** Points within `r s2$match_radius_m / 1000` km of a plot can sample habitat the plot does not represent.  Point counts in this analysis therefore represent a broader collection of habitats than CBBC plots that were selected within relatively uniform habitats.

The 95% intervals are sampling intervals: they take the NA-POPS corrections and CBBC densities as given, and do not include uncertainty in the corrections, which is dominated by EDR (Section \@ref(napops-corrections)). Section \@ref(ratio-caveats) sets out what moves the ratios.

**How this report is organized.** Section \@ref(main-results) gives the main results and Section \@ref(methods) the methods in brief. The checks on those results (Section \@ref(supporting)), the data behind them (Section \@ref(data-support)) and the NA-POPS corrections themselves (Section \@ref(napops-corrections)) follow. The appendix (Section \@ref(appendix)) has a worked example of the calculations, the data sources, how to reproduce the analysis and all the code.

# Main results {#main-results}

## NA-POPS-corrected point counts vs spot mapping {#plot-averaged}

**What this shows.** For each species, the mean NA-POPS-corrected point-count density across all its matched CBBC grids, divided by the mean CBBC territory density over the same grids (the plot-averaged density ratio; Section \@ref(methods-ratio)). Each plot contributes equally, however many surveys it has. Grids where spot mapping found no territories of a species add their corrected density to the numerator only, and the per-species table shows how much of each species' corrected density comes from them. Intervals come from the site bootstrap. A species with no birds counted gets a ratio of 0 with a degenerate interval here, so use its count-ratio interval instead (Section \@ref(observed-expected)).

```{r main-napops-tables}
bind_rows(
  `Comparable` = agreement_summary(df = filter(density_ratio, comparable)),
  `All species` = agreement_summary(df = density_ratio),
  .id = "subset"
) |>
  kable(digits = 2, col.names = c("Species", "Number of species", "Median density ratio", "Median fold difference (either direction)",
                                  "Share within 2x", "Share within 5x", "Share within 10x", "Median Spearman across plots"),
        caption = "Plot-averaged density ratio (corrected point-count density / CBBC density): median across species, median fold difference from agreement in either direction, share of species within 2x, 5x and 10x, and median within-species Spearman correlation across plots", label = "step3-density-ratio-1")

density_ratio |>
  filter(comparable) |>
  arrange(ratio) |>
  transmute(species,
            Grids                                  = n_sites,
            `Grids with CBBC territories`          = n_den_pos,
            `Mean CBBC density (/ km²)`            = round(den_mean, 1),
            `Mean corrected density (/ km²)`       = round(num_mean, 1),
            `Density ratio (95% sampling interval)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", ratio, ratio_lcl, ratio_ucl),
            `Corrected density from grids without CBBC territories` =
              if_else(condition = is.nan(share_zero_grids), true = "-", false = pct(share_zero_grids))) |>
  kable(caption = "Plot-averaged density ratio by comparable species, with its 95% site-bootstrap sampling interval, and the share of the species' summed corrected density that comes from grids where spot mapping found no territories of it",
        label = "step3-density-ratio-2")
```

```{r step3-density-ratio-plot, fig.cap = "Plot-averaged density ratio (corrected point-count density / CBBC density) by species, with 95% site-bootstrap sampling intervals.", fig.height = fig_height(nrow(density_ratio))}
plot_ratio(summary = density_ratio, xlab = "Plot-averaged density ratio: corrected point-count density / CBBC density")
```

```{r step3-density-means, fig.cap = "Species mean densities across all matched grids: NA-POPS-corrected point counts vs CBBC.", fig.height = 6}
plot_pair(df = density_ratio, x = "den_mean", y = "num_mean",
          xlab = "CBBC mean density (territories / km²)", ylab = "Point-count mean density, NA-POPS corrected (birds / km²)")
```

For comparable species, the median plot-averaged density ratio is **`r round(comp_density_ratio$median_ratio, 2)`**, with a median fold difference of `r round(comp_density_ratio$median_abs_fold, 2)` in either direction, `r pct(comp_density_ratio$within_2x)` of species within 2× of agreement and `r pct(comp_density_ratio$within_10x)` within 10×.

**How to read:**

- **Systematic bias vs scatter.** The median ratio shows whether corrected point counts run systematically above or below CBBC densities; the median fold difference shows how far individual species typically are from agreement in either direction. A median near 1 with large scatter means no overall bias but poor species-level agreement.
- **Grids without CBBC territories.** A large share of a species' corrected density from these grids means it was often counted near plots where spot mapping found none: either the points sample habitat the plot does not represent (most likely for edge and early-successional species), or the species colonized those plots after the census. Either way, its ratio is raised by something other than detectability.
- **Agreement across plots.** The median Spearman correlation across plots shows whether, within a species, corrected densities are higher where CBBC densities are higher. Each site's point-count density rests on few surveys (Table \@ref(tab:step1b-1)), so low correlations are expected even if the corrections are right.

## What the ratios do and do not show {#ratio-caveats}

A ratio of 1 means NA-POPS-corrected counts reproduce CBBC territory densities on average for that species. It does not, on its own, show that availability and EDR are right, because other things move the ratios:

- non-territorial birds contribute to point counts but not to spot-mapped territories
- spot mapping also misses some territories; point counts in this analysis often sample habitat the CBBC plot does not represent
- populations have changed in the several decades that elapsed between the CBBC and point count surveys

The detection-rate check (Section \@ref(supporting)) complements both ratios, because it compares how often surveys detect the species at all, which pairs and family groups do not inflate.

## PIF corrections instead of NA-POPS {#pif-vs-napops}

**Question.** Before NA-POPS, Partners in Flight (PIF) continental population estimates (Blancher et al. 2013; Stanton et al. 2019) converted Breeding Bird Survey counts to densities with two species-level corrections: a **time-of-day adjustment**, since replaced by NA-POPS availability, and a **maximum detection distance (MDD)**, since replaced by the NA-POPS EDR. Do the PIF corrections bring point counts closer to, or further from, what CBBC densities predict?

**How it is calculated.** Exactly as for NA-POPS: the same surveys, grids and CBBC densities; only each survey's effective area changes (Section \@ref(methods-pif)). Two hybrid corrections swap one component at a time, to show which replacement matters.

```{r main-pif-tables}
expected_vs_napops |>
  group_by(correction) |>
  summarise(median        = median(relative),
            q10           = quantile(relative, 0.10),
            q90           = quantile(relative, 0.90),
            share_above_1 = pct(mean(relative > 1)),
            .groups       = "drop") |>
  kable(digits = 2, col.names = c("Corrections", "Median", "10%", "90%", "Species with more birds expected than with NA-POPS"),
        caption = "Comparable species: birds expected with the PIF and hybrid corrections, relative to birds expected with NA-POPS (ratio of totals over each species' surveys). Above 1: the corrections assume the surveys sample more birds, so they give lower densities",
        label = "step3-pif-1")

kable(pif_agreement, digits = 2,
      col.names = c("Species", "Corrections", "Number of species", "Median density ratio", "Median fold difference (either direction)",
                    "Share within 2x", "Share within 5x", "Share within 10x", "Median Spearman across plots"),
      caption = "Plot-averaged density ratio (corrected point-count density / CBBC density) with NA-POPS, PIF and hybrid corrections, for the species with PIF values (same surveys and grids for every set)",
      label = "step3-pif-2")

pif_paired |>
  filter(comparable) |>
  arrange(r_napops) |>
  transmute(species,
            `Mean CBBC density (/ km²)`                  = round(den_mean, 1),
            `Density ratio, NA-POPS`                     = round(r_napops, 2),
            `Density ratio, PIF (95% sampling interval)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", r_pif, r_pif_lcl, r_pif_ucl),
            `Closer to 1`                                = coalesce(closer, "-"),
            `PIF time of day`                            = round(pif_tod, 2),
            `PIF MDD (m)`                                = pif_mdd_m,
            `NA-POPS EDR (m)`                            = round(edr_m),
            `PIF pair adjustment`                        = pif_pair) |>
  kable(caption = "Comparable species: plot-averaged density ratios with NA-POPS and PIF corrections, which is closer to agreement (1), and the corrections themselves (PIF time of day is for a 3-min BBS stop)",
        label = "step3-pif-4")
```

The species-by-species comparison of NA-POPS and PIF ratios is Figure \@ref(fig:summary-figure).

```{r step3-pif-means, fig.cap = "Species mean densities across all matched grids: NA-POPS-corrected (left) and PIF-corrected (right) point counts vs CBBC, species with PIF values. CBBC densities are the same in both panels; only the corrected densities change.", fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.5}
# As Figure \@ref(fig:step3-density-means), one panel per set of corrections
pif_density_ratio |>
  filter(correction %in% c("NA-POPS", "PIF")) |>
  plot_pair(x = "den_mean", y = "num_mean",
            xlab = "CBBC mean density (territories / km²)", ylab = "Point-count mean density, corrected (birds / km²)") +
  facet_wrap(facets = vars(correction))
```

`r n_pif_species` of the `r length(spp_napops)` species compared have PIF values. For comparable species, PIF corrections expect a median of **`r round(pif_rel_median, 2)` times** as many birds as NA-POPS (Table \@ref(tab:step3-pif-1)), so they give correspondingly lower corrected densities. The median plot-averaged density ratio is **`r round(pif_comp_pif$median_ratio, 2)`** with PIF corrections and **`r round(pif_comp_napops$median_ratio, 2)`** with NA-POPS, with median fold differences from agreement of `r round(pif_comp_pif$median_abs_fold, 2)` and `r round(pif_comp_napops$median_abs_fold, 2)`, and `r pct(pif_comp_pif$within_2x)` and `r pct(pif_comp_napops$within_2x)` of species within 2× of agreement, respectively (Table \@ref(tab:step3-pif-2)). PIF brings **`r n_closer_pif` of `r nrow(closer_comp)`** comparable species closer to agreement (`r pct(n_closer_pif / nrow(closer_comp))`; exact 95% interval `r pct(closer_ci[1])`-`r pct(closer_ci[2])`). With plots weighted by survey effort instead, the median count ratio is `r round(pif_count_comp$median_k[pif_count_comp$correction == "PIF"], 2)` with PIF and `r round(pif_count_comp$median_k[pif_count_comp$correction == "NA-POPS"], 2)` with NA-POPS (Table \@ref(tab:step3-pif-3)).

**How to read:**

- **Which way PIF moves the ratios.** In Table \@ref(tab:step3-pif-1), values above 1 mean PIF assumes the surveys sample more birds than NA-POPS does, which lowers corrected densities and the density ratio (and, in a population estimate, the population). In Figure \@ref(fig:step3-pif-means), this moves every species down from its NA-POPS position by about that factor: a factor shared by all species shifts the cloud of points off the 1:1 line without changing its scatter. The two hybrid rows split the difference into its two parts: time of day instead of availability, and MDD instead of EDR. Effective area grows with the square of the detection radius, so MDD vs EDR usually dominates for unlimited-distance counts, where it changes the area by (MDD / EDR)². For counts truncated at 50 or 100 m, both areas approach the truncation circle (π *r*²) when the radius is well beyond the limit, so the distance part shrinks.
- **Closer to 1 is not automatically better.** As Section \@ref(ratio-caveats) explains, the density ratio would sit below 1 even with perfect corrections if populations had declined since the census, and above 1 where pairs, fledglings and non-territorial birds are counted, or where points near a plot sample habitat the plot does not represent. A correction that moves ratios toward 1 is better only if those effects are small. In particular, if NA-POPS ratios already run above 1, PIF corrections can look better partly by offsetting the counting of individuals against territories, rather than by being better detectability corrections.
- **Hybrids.** If a hybrid agrees better than both full sets (Table \@ref(tab:step3-pif-2)), one component of each set is closer to the census than the other: for example, NA-POPS availability with PIF MDD agreeing best would point to EDR, not availability, as the source of any NA-POPS inflation.
- **Uncertainty.** As elsewhere, the intervals are sampling intervals that take the corrections as given. The PIF corrections carry no uncertainty here, and the time-of-day value refers to BBS timing rather than each BAM survey's own date and time.

# Methods in brief {#methods}

## Data and matching {#methods-data}

**Point counts.** Human point counts from the BAM database (no ARU recordings, no eBird checklists), within `r s2$match_radius_m / 1000` km of retained CBBC plots, in the breeding season and in the morning (filters in `P2_match_bam_surveys.R`; Table \@ref(tab:step1a-2)). All plots in coordinate groups containing multiple distinct CBBC SITEIDs were excluded before assignment, because their identical recorded positions cannot identify which historical plot nearby surveys represent. Among the initially survey-matched plots, this excluded **`r n_shared_sites_excluded` plots in `r n_shared_groups_excluded` coordinate groups**; **`r n_matched` uniquely located CBBC sites** remain. Each retained BAM survey is assigned once to its nearest eligible plot *in P2*, before species selection.

**Why spot mapping.** CBBC observers visited each plot repeatedly (at least the minimum number of visits set in P1; Table \@ref(tab:step1a-1)) and mapped territories, so CBBC densities are territories per unit area, including fractions of territories crossing the plot edge, with no detectability correction involved. For territorial songbirds detected mainly by song, this is approximately the quantity a corrected point count estimates. The two are not identical: point counts record individuals (which may include non-territorial individuals), whereas spot mapping records territories. Spot mapping also misses some territories, so CBBC is treated as an independent reference rather than the truth.

**Sites compared.** Every comparison uses the final matched, coordinate-unambiguous CBBC sites for every species, including sites where spot mapping found no territories of that species (CBBC density 0). The species occurrence threshold is also evaluated on exactly these final sites. Two things argue for including sites with CBBC zeros:

- **No selection on the outcome.** Keeping only grids where spot mapping found a species selects grids where its CBBC density was high partly by chance, and biases CBBC densities upward relative to the point counts.
- **Turnover since the census.** Over the decades between the censuses and the point counts, species were lost from some plots and gained at others. Keeping only grids where the species held territories at the census keeps the losses but discards the gains, which biases point-count densities downward. Including all retained sites allows both apparent losses and gains to contribute, although spatially heterogeneous change, imperfect census coverage and habitat differences remain.

The cost is habitat mismatch: points within `r s2$match_radius_m / 1000` km of a plot can sample habitat the plot does not represent (for example, edges or young forest around a mature-forest plot), so a species can be counted near a plot where spot mapping found none.

## Species compared {#species-compared}

**Scope.** Species are selected if CBBC territories were recorded at **`r s3$min_sites_cbbc` or more of the `r n_matched` final, uniquely located sites** (set in P3), and an NA-POPS model is available, without which counts cannot be corrected. Nothing about BAM detections, availability or EDR is used to determine eligibility, so no species is included or excluded because of how well BAM and CBBC agree. All eligible species are retained, but **only comparable species contribute to the primary density-agreement summaries**. The biologically motivated, judgment-based classification is defined centrally in P1 (`NON_COMPARABLE_SPECIES`; Section \@ref(settings-used)) and distinguishes species with readily interpreted breeding territories from those whose point-count detections cannot reliably be assigned to a comparable local territory. This is a statement about the compatibility of the two measurements, not about the quality of either survey method.

`r length(spp_primary)` of `r nrow(species_selection)` candidate species have NA-POPS models and are compared (`r sum(species_selection$primary & species_selection$comparable)` comparable, `r sum(species_selection$primary & !species_selection$comparable)` non-comparable). `r sum(species_selection$primary & !species_selection$detected_nearby)` of them were never detected by a matched BAM survey. The species are listed in Table \@ref(tab:step1-species-2).


### Why particular species are classified as non-comparable {#noncomparable-justifications}

The following table covers **every code flagged as non-comparable in P1**, including species that do not meet the occurrence threshold in the current run. The reason is specifically why birds recorded on short point counts may not correspond closely to the density of breeding territories inferred from repeated spot mapping. Some of these birds do defend nests or territories; the flag does **not** mean they are wholly nonterritorial. The classification is a conservative ecological judgment made independently of the observed/expected ratios.

```{r noncomparable-rationale-table}
noncomparable_rationale <- tribble(
  ~species, ~common_name, ~reason,
  "AMCR", "American Crow", "Family groups and broad, mobile foraging ranges can extend well beyond a small mapped breeding plot.",
  "AMGO", "American Goldfinch", "Loose territoriality, flocking and late/variable nesting make birds counted locally hard to pair with fixed mapped territories.",
  "BANS", "Bank Swallow", "Colonial burrow nesting and extensive aerial foraging decouple local flight counts from nesting territories.",
  "BARS", "Barn Swallow", "Defends nest sites but forages widely on the wing; birds passing a point may nest elsewhere.",
  "BHCO", "Brown-headed Cowbird", "Brood parasite: females do not hold a conventional nesting territory, and birds visit multiple host territories.",
  "BLJA", "Blue Jay", "Broad, overlapping home ranges and inconspicuous territorial boundaries make spot-mapped units hard to match to point-count birds.",
  "CEDW", "Cedar Waxwing", "Social flocks, mobile feeding and relatively weak nesting-area defence make detections poor indicators of local territories.",
  "CHSW", "Chimney Swift", "Nest-site-focused defence and wide-ranging aerial feeding mean birds overhead may not breed locally.",
  "CLSW", "Cliff Swallow", "Dense nesting colonies and wide aerial feeding movements make counts of flying birds unlike mapped territory counts.",
  "COGR", "Common Grackle", "Often nests in loose groups and mainly defends the nest vicinity; birds forage well beyond it.",
  "CORA", "Common Raven", "Very large territories and far-ranging movements exceed the scale of most CBBC plots.",
  "EUST", "European Starling", "Primarily defends nest cavities and feeds in mobile groups; observed birds need not belong to nests on the plot.",
  "EVGR", "Evening Grosbeak", "Flocking, nomadic movements and weakly exclusive breeding areas complicate assignment to local territories.",
  "HOSP", "House Sparrow", "Groups nest around buildings, defending mainly nest sites while sharing feeding areas.",
  "MODO", "Mourning Dove", "Defends a localized nesting area but may travel far to feed; point-count birds need not occupy a local nesting territory.",
  "NOFL", "Northern Flicker", "Nest-site defence and extensive ground-foraging movements can place counted birds far from their nesting areas.",
  "NRWS", "Northern Rough-winged Swallow", "Defends nesting burrows but feeds widely in flight; aerial detections are poorly tied to local nests.",
  "PISI", "Pine Siskin", "Irruptive, often flocking and mobile, with variable breeding locations and weakly exclusive feeding areas.",
  "PUMA", "Purple Martin", "Often nests in colonies or clustered cavities and forages widely in the air, so local flight counts differ from nesting sites.",
  "RECR", "Red Crossbill", "Nomadic, flocking and opportunistic breeding tied to seed crops makes fixed territory density a poor comparison.",
  "ROPI", "Rock Pigeon", "Colonial or clustered nesting and wide-ranging flock foraging make point-count birds poorly attributable to local nests.",
  "RUGR", "Ruffed Grouse", "Males have drumming territories, but peak drumming is usually earlier than the May–July point-count window; females and non-drumming birds are sampled differently.",
  "TRES", "Tree Swallow", "Defends a nest cavity while feeding broadly in flight; detections at a point need not represent local breeding pairs.",
  "WWCR", "White-winged Crossbill", "Nomadic flocks and opportunistic conifer-seed-driven breeding make a fixed, exclusive territory hard to enumerate."
)

# Fail loudly if someone edits the classification in P1 without updating its
# corresponding explanation here, or vice versa.
if (anyDuplicated(noncomparable_rationale$species) ||
    !setequal(noncomparable_rationale$species, s1$non_comparable_species)) {
  stop("README species justifications and P1 NON_COMPARABLE_SPECIES differ. Update both before knitting.")
}

noncomparable_rationale |>
  mutate(`In this run` = if_else(species %in% spp_primary, "Yes", "No")) |>
  arrange(desc(`In this run` == "Yes"), common_name) |>
  select(Species = species, `Common name` = common_name, `In this run`,
         `Why point counts and mapped territories may differ` = reason) |>
  kable(caption = "Ecological justifications for every species flagged non-comparable in P1 (including species not eligible in this run)",
        label = "noncomparable-rationales")
```

## How point counts are compared with CBBC {#methods-ratio}

**Effective area.** NA-POPS converts a point count to a density by dividing it by the area the survey effectively sampled. For survey *j*:

> *A*~*j*~ = *p*~*j*~ × π × EDR² × (1 − exp(−(*r*~*j*~ / EDR)²)) / 10^6^ (km²)

where *p*~*j*~ is availability, the probability that a bird present sings or calls during the count (NA-POPS removal model; it depends on the survey's duration, day of year and time since sunrise), EDR is the species' effective detection radius (m; NA-POPS intercept-only distance model), and *r*~*j*~ is the survey's distance limit (m). For an unlimited-distance count the last factor is 1.

**Plot-averaged density ratio (main comparison).** For each species and CBBC grid *g*, the corrected point-count density is *B*~*g*~ = Σ count / Σ *A*~*j*~ over the surveys assigned to the grid. The CBBC density *D*~*g*~ is territories on the plot divided by plot area, averaged over the grid's census years. The species' ratio is *R* = mean(*B*~*g*~) / mean(*D*~*g*~) over all its matched grids, so *R* = 1 means corrected point counts reproduce CBBC territory densities on average. Every plot gets equal weight, whatever its number of surveys. That matters here because survey effort ranges from one survey to well over 100 per site (Table \@ref(tab:step1b-1)).

**Count ratio (check).** Birds counted divided by birds expected, Σ count / Σ (*A*~*j*~ × *D*~*g*~), over the species' surveys. It is the maximum-likelihood estimate under a Poisson model, but weights each plot by its survey effort, so one heavily surveyed plot can dominate it.

**Intervals.** The 95% sampling intervals come from a site bootstrap: sites are resampled with all their surveys, so repeat visits and nearby points move together. They describe how much the results depend on which sites and surveys happened to be available, taking the NA-POPS corrections and the CBBC densities as given. They do not include uncertainty in the corrections themselves (model choice, NA-POPS release, availability), error in the historical CBBC densities, population change or spatial mismatch. Because density scales with 1 / EDR² for unlimited-distance counts, errors in EDR dominate that uncertainty (Section \@ref(napops-corrections)).

The appendix (Section \@ref(absolute-logic)) works through both ratios with a small invented example, and explains how plot size and survey effort enter them.

## PIF corrections {#methods-pif}

PIF converts counts to densities with a time-of-day adjustment instead of availability, and a maximum detection distance (MDD) instead of EDR. The PIF effective area (computed in `P4_pif_corrections.R`) is:

> *A*~*j*~^PIF^ = *p*~*j*~^PIF^ × π × MDD² × (1 − exp(−(*r*~*j*~ / MDD)²)) / 10^6^

- **MDD** (m) is the PIF detection distance, treated here as an expert-elicited estimate of the species' EDR, so the formula is the NA-POPS one with MDD in place of EDR. Despite the name "maximum detection distance", PIF uses it as the radius of the area a count samples (π × MDD²), the role EDR plays in NA-POPS. The PIF handbook (version 3.1) acknowledges that not all birds within that distance are detected, notes that its distance classes tend to run larger than empirical effective detection distances, and names replacing them with EDRs as the next step. With the same half-normal detection function for both, PIF and NA-POPS differ only in the value of the radius. For unlimited-distance counts the area is *p*~*j*~^PIF^ × π × MDD².
- ***p*~*j*~^PIF^** comes from the PIF time-of-day value *T*: the share of birds counted at the mean BBS time of day relative to the species' peak time, on a 3-min BBS stop. BAM surveys last 3 to 10 min, so *T* is rescaled to each survey's duration *d* (min) assuming a constant cue rate, *p*^PIF^ = 1 − (1 − *T*)^*d*/3^, the same rescaling used for the 5-min availability in Table \@ref(tab:step1-species-2) (setting `pif_scale_duration` in P4: **`r s4$pif_scale_duration`**; if FALSE, *T* is used unchanged for every survey). Unlike NA-POPS availability, it does not change with date or time since sunrise.
- **The PIF pair adjustment is not used.** PIF multiplies densities by a pair adjustment (1 to 2) to convert birds counted to individuals. NA-POPS did not replace it, and both comparisons here set birds counted against territories, so leaving it out means any difference between the NA-POPS and PIF ratios comes only from the two corrections that NA-POPS replaced. Species with a pair adjustment below 2 are, by PIF's own reckoning, counted as more than one bird per territory (both sexes, or family groups), so their ratios should run above 1 under either set of corrections.
- **Hybrids.** To show which replacement matters, two hybrid corrections swap one component at a time: PIF time of day with the NA-POPS EDR, and NA-POPS availability with the PIF MDD.

Corrections that assume a survey samples more birds give lower corrected densities, a lower density ratio, and smaller populations. For one species, the PIF count ratio divided by the NA-POPS count ratio equals birds expected with NA-POPS divided by birds expected with PIF. The plot-averaged density ratio moves by about the same factor, though not exactly, because the PIF / NA-POPS effective-area ratio varies somewhat between surveys of one species (with duration and distance limit).

# Supporting analyses and robustness checks {#supporting}

These analyses check whether the main results depend on how plots are weighted, on how many birds are recorded per detection, on the time since the census and on plot characteristics, and compare species composition.

## Count ratio: plots weighted by survey effort {#observed-expected}

**What this shows.** For each species, the total number of birds counted by its surveys divided by the total expected from CBBC density and each survey's NA-POPS effective area (the observed and expected counts of Table \@ref(tab:step1-species-2)). It weights each grid by its survey effort multiplied by its CBBC density, so it checks whether the plot-averaged result holds when every survey counts equally, and shows where a few heavily surveyed grids dominate.

```{r check-count-tables}
bind_rows(
  `Comparable` = count_ratio_agreement(df = filter(count_ratio, comparable)),
  `All species` = count_ratio_agreement(df = count_ratio),
  .id = "subset"
) |>
  kable(digits = 2, col.names = c("Species", "Number of species", "Median count ratio", "Median fold difference (either direction)",
                                  "Share within 2x", "Share within 5x", "Species with no birds counted"),
        caption = "Count ratio (birds counted / birds expected): median across species, median fold difference from agreement in either direction, and share of species within 2x and 5x of agreement", label = "step3-count-ratio-1")

count_ratio |>
  filter(comparable) |>
  arrange(k) |>
  transmute(species,
            Grids                         = n_sites,
            `Grids with CBBC territories` = n_sites_cbbc,
            Surveys                       = n_surveys,
            `Birds counted`               = observed,
            `Birds expected`              = round(expected, 1),
            `Count ratio (95% sampling interval)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", k, k_lcl, k_ucl),
            `Largest site's share of expected`    = pct(max_site_share)) |>
  kable(caption = "Count ratio by comparable species, with its 95% sampling interval (wider of the site bootstrap and the exact Poisson interval), and the share of the expected count contributed by the species' single largest site (a large share means one site dominates the ratio)", label = "step3-count-ratio-2")
```

For comparable species, the median count ratio is **`r round(comp_count_ratio$median_k, 2)`**, with `r pct(comp_count_ratio$within_2x)` of species within 2× of agreement and a median fold difference of `r round(comp_count_ratio$median_abs_fold, 2)` in either direction, compared with a median plot-averaged density ratio of `r round(comp_density_ratio$median_ratio, 2)`.

**How to read:** where one site supplies most of a species' expected count, its count ratio mostly reflects that site, and its interval is unreliable (Section \@ref(absolute-logic)). A count ratio well above the plot-averaged density ratio usually means heavily surveyed grids, or grids without CBBC territories that have many surveys, contribute many birds. The next section lists the species where the two ratios differ by more than 2×.

## When the two ratios disagree

**What this shows.** Species whose count ratio and plot-averaged density ratio differ by more than 2×. For these, the two ways of weighting plots give different answers, usually because one or two heavily surveyed sites dominate the count ratio.

```{r step3-ratio-compare, fig.cap = "Count ratio vs plot-averaged density ratio, by species. Line: the two ratios agree; dashed lines: 2x apart.", fig.height = 6}
ratio_pairs |>
  filter(count_ratio > 0, density_ratio > 0) |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = density_ratio, y = count_ratio, colour = species_class, shape = species_class)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_abline(intercept = log10(c(0.5, 2)), slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(mapping = aes(label = species), size = 2.2, vjust = -0.7, check_overlap = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = CLASS_COLOURS) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = CLASS_SHAPES) +
  labs(x = "Plot-averaged density ratio", y = "Count ratio", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

ratio_pairs |>
  filter(is.finite(fold_apart), abs(log(fold_apart)) > log(2)) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(log(fold_apart)))) |>
  transmute(species,
            `Grids with CBBC territories` = n_sites_cbbc,
            `Plot-averaged density ratio` = round(density_ratio, 2),
            `Count ratio` = round(count_ratio, 2),
            `Largest site's share of expected` = pct(max_site_share)) |>
  kable(caption = "Species whose count ratio and plot-averaged density ratio differ by more than 2x, with the share of the expected count contributed by the species' largest site", label = "step3-ratio-compare-1")
```

**How to read:** points near the line mean the result does not depend on how plots are weighted. For species in the table, one site often supplies a large share of the expected count, so the count ratio mostly describes that site; the plot-averaged density ratio, the main comparison, is the fairer summary of the species.

## PIF corrections: count-ratio check

The PIF comparison of Section \@ref(pif-vs-napops), repeated with the count ratio, which weights plots by survey effort.

```{r check-pif-count}
kable(pif_count_agreement, digits = 2,
      col.names = c("Species", "Corrections", "Number of species", "Median count ratio", "Median fold difference (either direction)",
                    "Share within 2x", "Share within 5x", "Species with no birds counted"),
      caption = "Check: count ratio (birds counted / birds expected) with NA-POPS, PIF and hybrid corrections, for the species with PIF values (same surveys and grids for every set)",
      label = "step3-pif-3")
```

## Detection-rate check

**What this tests.** A second check that is insensitive to how many birds were recorded per detection. If CBBC density and the NA-POPS corrections were both right, a survey with effective area *a* would detect the species (count at least one bird) with probability 1 − exp(−D~CBBC~ × *a*). The observed share of surveys detecting the species is compared with this expectation. It is evaluated per survey, not per grid, because repeat visits to the same point re-survey the same birds. At grids where spot mapping found no territories the expected detection rate is 0, so any detection there counts as excess.

```{r step3-detection, fig.cap = "Detection-rate check, comparable species at all matched grids: observed vs expected share of surveys detecting the species."}
kable(detection_summary, digits = 2,
      caption = "Detection-rate check at all matched grids (comparable species): observed vs expected share of surveys detecting the species", label = "step3-detection-1")

ggplot(data = detection_check, mapping = aes(x = detect_exp, y = detect_obs)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(colour = CLASS_COLOURS[["Comparable"]], shape = CLASS_SHAPES[["Comparable"]]) +
  geom_text(mapping = aes(label = species), size = 2.2, vjust = -0.7, check_overlap = TRUE) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Expected share of surveys detecting the species (CBBC density x NA-POPS area)",
       y = "Observed share of surveys detecting the species",
       caption = "Line: agreement") +
  theme_bw()
```
